Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the call on Friday. As discussed, we’ve drafted a short mutual action plan (MAP) to align technical owners and close timelines for the evaluation. I’m looping in our Solutions Engineer, Dylan, and our ML engineer, Neha, who will co-lead the technical kickoff and evaluation cadence.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Hi Alyssa / Shea —

Great — thanks for confirming. Wed 8/12 9:00–9:45am PST works for us; I’ve penciled it in. I’m attaching a short evaluation checklist (evaluation-plan.xlsx) that breaks down the 4-week run:

Week 0 (kickoff & infra prep) — connectivity, keys, sample dataset setup
Week 1 (pilot) — functional validation, sample throughput tests, basic prompt coverage
Week 2 (performance) — latency and cost runs (with batching/quantization profiles)
Week 3 (integration) — KV/prefix caching verification, failover scenarios, and production smoke tests

Addressing Alyssa’s asks:
- SOC2/data retention: Neha has a one-pager that outlines data flows and retention defaults for hosted vs dedicated. Neha — I’ll let you paste that in the thread.
- Infra sizing: for a small pilot we recommend 1x A10 / equivalent for throughput testing and a single T4-equivalent for smoke tests if you want to keep cost low. If you expect long sequences (>2k tokens) we should size up to an A100 class. We’ll include rough hourly cost estimates in the checklist.

Agenda for Wed 9:00–9:45am PST:
1) Introductions & success criteria (5m)
2) Architecture overview & access plan (10m)
3) Evaluation checklist walkthrough (15m)
4) Data handling & security Q&A (10m)
5) Next steps & owners (5m)

Attachments:
- evaluation-plan.xlsx (detailed checklist and cost appendix)

See you Wednesday — I’ll post a calendar invite shortly.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

Subject: Data retention & logging summary (SOC2 items)

Hi Alyssa / Shea —

Per Marcus’ note, here’s a concise summary of the evaluation-specific data handling defaults you asked for:

- Request data: by default, hosted evaluation requests are retained for 30 days for debugging and quality monitoring; logs are hashed and access-controlled.
- KV / prefix cache: ephemeral in-memory caches on the serving nodes; cached values are not persisted to disk in hosted evaluations. For Dedicated, cache persistence is configurable per-customer; we can set retention to 0 days for strict no-persistence.
- Audit logs: request metadata (timestamps, model id, latency) retained for 90 days; content-level data redaction is available on request.
- Encryption & keys: all data in transit is TLS 1.2+; customer-managed keys supported for Private/Dedicated deployments (KMS/HSM).

If you need a signed SOC2 artifact, we can route a request through our compliance portal — I attached the SOC2-summary-redwood.pdf for initial review.

Happy to discuss any of this on the kickoff; Dylan — please call out any infra caveats.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
